extracted.intended_audience: registered patent attorneys/practitioners before the USPTO, counsel for respondents, and USPTO OED personnel
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive rules governing interim suspension of a practitioner from practice before the USPTO under 37 C.F.R. § 11.25, including notice, response, referral for formal proceedings, limited recognition, publication, and operational consequences (Customer Numbers/PKI).

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for interim suspension (serious crime/felony)
rubrics_metrics.description: Interim suspension may be imposed predicated on evidence that Respondent committed a serious crime, which was a felony offense (e.g., violation of 15 U.S.C. § 1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order was issued pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.25 based on Respondent's guilty plea to two counts of conspiracy to fix prices (a felony). A felony conviction is treated as sufficient evidence of a 'serious crime' to justify interim suspension under § 11.25.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice and Order delivery and content
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'Notice and Order Pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.25' must be mailed (certified mail in this case) to the address of Respondent's counsel provided to the OED Director and delivered to Respondent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Notice and Order must inform the respondent of the OED Director's request for interim suspension and of the attached Disciplinary Complaint; it should provide the respondent with the opportunity to respond within the regulatory period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opportunity to respond within forty (40) days
rubrics_metrics.description: The Notice and Order provided Respondent an opportunity to file, within forty (40) days, a response containing information sufficient to establish a genuine issue of material fact based upon any of the grounds permissible under 37 C.F.R. § 11.25(b)(3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A timely response must raise a genuine issue of material fact under the cited regulation to avoid interim suspension; failure to file a response within the 40-day period supports a determination that no genuine issue exists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Default standard when no response is filed
rubrics_metrics.description: In light of Respondent's failure to file a response, the Director determined there is no genuine issue of material fact under 37 C.F.R. § 11.25(b), and interim suspension and referral for formal proceedings is appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to respond to the Notice and Order may be treated as concession that no factual dispute exists, permitting immediate interim suspension under § 11.25(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope and effective date of interim suspension
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall be suspended on an interim basis from the practice of patent, trademark, and other non-patent law before the USPTO in accordance with 37 C.F.R. § 11.25(b), effective the date of this Final Order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The suspension is effective immediately upon issuance of the Final Order and covers all practice before the Office (patent, trademark, and other non-patent matters) as specified by the regulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limited recognition to practice to facilitate compliance with §11.58(b)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent is granted limited recognition to practice before the Office commencing on the date of this Order and expiring thirty (30) days after the date this Order is signed, with such limited recognition being granted for the sole purpose of facilitating Respondent's compliance with the provisions of 37 C.F.R. § 11.58(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limited recognition is narrowly tailored (30 days) and is only to permit the suspended practitioner to take steps required by § 11.58(b) (e.g., notices to clients and winding up pending matters).

rubrics_metrics.name: Referral of Disciplinary Complaint for formal disciplinary proceeding
rubrics_metrics.description: The Disciplinary Complaint is referred, in accordance with 37 C.F.R. § 11.25(b)(5), to a hearing officer (here, at the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development) for the purpose of conducting a formal disciplinary proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Referral starts the formal process under the cited regulation; the hearing officer will preside over the respondent's answer and the evidentiary/disciplinary process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to file written answer within thirty (30) days under §11.36
rubrics_metrics.description: Pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.36, within thirty (30) days from the date of this Final Order, Respondent's written answer to the Disciplinary Complaint shall be filed with the hearing officer at the specified addresses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The order supplies both mail and hand-delivery addresses for the HUD Office of Hearings and Appeals Docket Clerk, and requires a PDF version of the answer to be filed via email with the hearing office; a copy must also be served on the OED Director at the specified mailing address (Sydney O. Johnson, Senior Counsel for Enrollment and Discipline). Compliance with the filing methods and deadlines of § 11.36 is mandatory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service and filing procedures and addresses
rubrics_metrics.description: If sent by mail or hand-delivery, the answer must be addressed to the Docket Clerk at the HUD Office of Hearings and Appeals at the specified mail and hand-delivery addresses; a PDF must be emailed to the hearing office, and a copy served on the OED Director by mail to the provided OED address.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strict adherence to the provided addresses and electronic filing instruction is required for proper service; failure to serve as directed may affect the proceeding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of Notice of Interim Suspension in the Official Gazette
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall publish a Notice of Interim Suspension in the Official Gazette identifying the practitioner (name and registration number), stating the interim suspension and the basis (here, conviction for violations of Section 1 of the Sherman Antitrust Act), and noting the statutory/regulatory authority (35 U.S.C. § 32; 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.25 and 11.59).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The notice is to be posted for public reading and made available via the OED Reading Room/FOIA link; the notice should include sufficient factual information to identify the basis for suspension and the practitioner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice to USPTO, government entities, and state bar authorities
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall give notice of this Final Order to (i) appropriate employees of the USPTO; (ii) interested departments, agencies, and courts of the United States; and (iii) appropriate authorities of any state in which Respondent is known to be a member of the bar.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The dissemination requirement ensures relevant internal and external authorities are informed of the interim suspension for administrative and reciprocal discipline purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to comply with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 11.58 sets out duties of suspended practitioners (e.g., notices to clients, withdrawal from representation, protection of client interests); the Final Order expressly requires compliance with those duties during the suspension period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dissociation from Customer Numbers and PKI certificate
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO shall dissociate Respondent's name from any Customer Numbers and the public key infrastructure ('PKI') certificate associated with those Customer Numbers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operational measures will be taken to prevent the suspended practitioner from using USPTO electronic systems tied to Customer Numbers/PKI during suspension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on obtaining or being added to USPTO Customer Numbers while suspended
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall not apply for a USPTO Customer Number, shall not obtain a USPTO Customer Number, nor shall he have his name added to a USPTO Customer number, unless and until he is reinstated to practice before the USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This provision prevents circumvention of the suspension by re-registering or piggybacking onto others' Customer Numbers; reinstatement is required before access may be restored.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of seeking review on the suspension (no stay)
rubrics_metrics.description: If Respondent seeks a review of this suspension, any review shall not operate to postpone or otherwise hold in abeyance the suspension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing for review or appeal does not automatically stay the interim suspension; the suspension remains in effect during any review unless a separate stay is granted.
